{
  "focal_prediction": "In a synthetic planning fixture with a shifting bottleneck, adaptive allocation will produce better net service performance than a fixed allocation under the same reserve-capacity budget and disruption draws.",
  "rival_prediction": "Once reserve-capacity spending is matched, adaptive allocation will not improve net service performance over fixed allocation; any apparent gain from greater reserve spending will disappear.",
  "comparison": "Propose a paired simulation experiment in which both methods face the same sequence of disruptions and bottleneck shifts. The adaptive method reallocates reserve capacity in response to the observed bottleneck; the fixed method uses a prespecified allocation. Compare paired net service performance, accounting for switching cost and activation latency.",
  "matched_resource_budget": "Give each method the same total reserve-capacity budget over each paired run and require equal reserve-capacity expenditure. Record expenditure to verify the match.",
  "controls": [
    "Use identical disruption draws, initial conditions, demand, and bottleneck-shift sequences within each pair.",
    "Prespecify the fixed allocation and the adaptive reallocation rule before evaluating outcomes.",
    "Apply the same measurement definitions and cost accounting to both methods.",
    "Include a stable-bottleneck condition to check whether any adaptive advantage is specific to shifting bottlenecks.",
    "Verify that the intended bottleneck shifts occur and that both methods' resource expenditures and outcomes are measured correctly."
  ],
  "observable": "The paired difference in net service performance, using a prespecified service metric and deducting switching costs; also record activation latency, switching cost, and reserve-capacity expenditure for each method.",
  "falsifier": "The focal prediction is not supported if, in valid shifting-bottleneck runs with matched reserve expenditure, the prespecified paired comparison shows no improvement in net service performance for adaptive allocation.",
  "inconclusive_condition": "The outcome is inconclusive if the bottleneck-shift manipulation, budget matching, or measurement controls fail, or if the prespecified comparison cannot distinguish an improvement from no improvement.",
  "stopping_rule": "Before any run, specify the number of paired disruption sequences, the service metric, and the decision threshold. Stop after that fixed number of pairs; do not extend the experiment based on interim results.",
  "execution_status": "Proposal only, using a synthetic planning fixture. No dataset, simulation, or run exists; this is not permission to execute a study or change a frozen scientific plan."
}

  "rival_prediction": "With total reserve capacity and disruption draws matched, the adaptive and static-reserve arms would not differ; any gain would track reserve capacity/spend rather than adaptation, so the shifting-minus-stable difference-in-differences would be zero.",
  "comparison": "2x2 between-arm/between-regime contrast: mechanism (adaptive vs matched static reserve) × bottleneck regime (shifting vs stable). Primary estimate is difference-in-differences: (adaptive − static | shifting) − (adaptive − static | stable). Within each regime, both arms receive identical disruption draw IDs and identical total reserve-capacity budgets. Activation latency and switching cost are logged but not used to add reserve.",
  "matched_resource_budget": "All arms and regimes receive the same total reserve-capacity units per episode, same episode length, same evaluation windows, and identical disruption draw IDs within regime; no extra reserve, episodes, or draws are given to any arm. Any timing differences in reserve release are logged as part of the mechanism and audited against total spend.",
  "controls": [
    "Manipulation check: verify scheduled bottleneck shifts occur and are observable in logs; if shifts are absent or undetected, outcome is inconclusive.",
    "Measurement control: independent audit that total reserve units spent and disruption draw IDs match across arms within regime; mismatch makes outcome inconclusive.",
    "Static-reserve control receives the same bottleneck information but uses a fixed non-adaptive allocation rule, isolating adaptation from information access.",
    "Stable-bottleneck negative control tests for generic effort or latency effects; H1 predicts attenuated adaptive advantage there.",
    "Record activation latency and switching cost for every arm; missing or unrecordable values make outcome inconclusive.",
    "Pre-specify primary outcome and analysis; no outcome-dependent stopping or reanalysis."
  ],
  "observable": "Primary: normalized allocation regret over post-shift evaluation blocks (lower is better), computed from logged bottleneck state, allocations, and completion/loss. Secondary: post-shift reallocation accuracy, activation latency, switching cost, and audited total reserve spend. No values are asserted because no run exists.",
  "falsifier": "H1 would be falsified if, with all controls passing and reserve/disruption draws matched, the adaptive arm fails to outperform the matched static-reserve arm under shifting bottleneck, or the shifting-minus-stable difference-in-differences is not positive, or any apparent advantage is fully attributable to logged reserve spend rather than post-shift reallocation. H2 would be falsified by a positive adaptive advantage under matched reserve spend and matched disruption draws.",
  "inconclusive_condition": "Outcome is inconclusive if the bottleneck-shift manipulation check fails, the reserve-spend or disruption-draw matching audit fails, activation latency or switching cost cannot be recorded, primary outcome logs are missing or invalid, or the stable-bottleneck control is not stable. No empirical claim is made in that case.",
  "stopping_rule": "Single fixed-horizon run with a pre-specified number of disruption blocks per arm per regime (proposed design horizon: 32 blocks per arm per regime), no interim efficacy looks and no optional stopping. Stop early only for a failed control check and label the result inconclusive; do not extend or re-run based on observed outcome.",
  "execution_status": "proposal_only; synthetic planning fixture; not executed; no dataset, simulation, or run exists; not permission, approval, or a frozen-plan change."
}

  "focal_prediction": "Across 40 paired synthetic disruption draws, the adaptive mechanism will have lower mean allocation loss than a nonadaptive comparator that fixes reserve allocation using the initial bottleneck. Both policies receive and deploy exactly the same reserve capacity; the adaptive policy will shift reserve toward the new bottleneck after each scheduled shift. Positive paired improvement under these conditions supports adaptation to the shifting bottleneck rather than additional reserve spending.",
  "rival_prediction": "With reserve deployment and disruption draws matched, the adaptive mechanism will show no allocation-loss advantage. Any advantage observed without matched deployment would instead be attributable to greater reserve-capacity spending.",
  "comparison": "Run one fixed-horizon, 100-period paired comparison per draw, with bottleneck shifts at periods 25, 50, and 75. The primary estimand is the mean paired difference: nonadaptive allocation loss minus adaptive allocation loss, so positive values favor the focal mechanism. Report a 95% paired confidence interval; no tuning or additional draws are permitted.",
  "matched_resource_budget": {
    "reserve_capacity": "The same pre-specified capacity-period budget B for each policy within each paired draw; both must deploy exactly B, differing only in allocation timing and location.",
    "disruptions": "Identical disruption draws, initial conditions, demand, capacities, and bottleneck-shift sequence through common random seeds.",
    "other_resources": "Identical activation-latency functions, switching-cost functions, and scoring rules."
  },
  "controls": [
    "Verify that each scheduled bottleneck shift occurs and is observable to the adaptive policy.",
    "Verify that the nonadaptive policy does not reallocate after initialization and that the adaptive policy reallocates toward the measured bottleneck.",
    "Audit per-draw reserve deployment for exact budget equality and reject any pair with a mismatch.",
    "Calculate allocation loss identically for both policies, with activation delays reducing delivered capacity and switching penalties included.",
    "Record activation latency and switching cost for every activation and switch, alongside reserve locations and bottleneck measurements.",
    "Use fixed policies, horizon, draw count, and analysis before execution."
  ],
  "observable": {
    "primary": "Total allocation loss over the fixed horizon under the common scoring rule.",
    "mechanism_check": "Post-shift reserve share assigned to the currently measured bottleneck.",
    "required_logs": "Reserve deployment by period and location, activation latencies, switching costs, disruption seeds, and paired allocation losses."
  },
  "falsifier": "The focal prediction is falsified in this experiment if mean paired improvement is zero or negative, or if the adaptive policy fails to move reserve toward shifted bottlenecks. The rival prediction is falsified if the adaptive policy achieves a positive improvement whose 95% confidence interval excludes zero while reserve deployment and all paired controls remain matched.",
  "inconclusive_condition": "The outcome is inconclusive if any manipulation or measurement control fails, including unequal reserve deployment, mismatched disruption draws, absent or unobserved bottleneck shifts, failed policy-behavior checks, inconsistent loss measurement, or missing latency or switching-cost logs. A confidence interval crossing zero also does not establish a confirmed adaptive advantage.",
  "stopping_rule": "Stop after exactly 40 valid paired draws and conduct the single pre-specified analysis. Do not add draws based on results. Stop early and declare the experiment inconclusive if a control failure cannot be corrected without changing the pre-specified design.",
  "execution_status": "Proposal only; not permission to execute. No dataset, simulation, experimental run, or empirical result exists."
}

  "focal_prediction": "In a bounded software-fixture experiment with shifting bottlenecks, an adaptive allocation policy will achieve better task performance or faster recovery than a capacity-matched nonadaptive policy, even when both receive identical total reserve capacity and identical disruption draws. The focal advantage should remain after recording activation latency and switching cost.",
  "rival_prediction": "Under identical total reserve-capacity budgets and disruption draws, the adaptive policy will not outperform the capacity-matched nonadaptive policy once reserve spending is matched. Any observed gain should be attributable to differences in reserve consumption rather than adaptation to the shifting bottleneck.",
  "comparison": "Run paired episodes using the same initial state and replayed disruption trace. In one condition, the focal policy reallocates reserve capacity in response to the currently measured bottleneck. In the rival condition, reserve capacity follows a prespecified nonadaptive allocation schedule with the same total budget and the same allowed reserve-spending opportunities. Compare task performance, recovery time, and disruption impact between paired episodes, while separately accounting for activation latency and switching cost.",
  "matched_resource_budget": "Each paired condition receives the same fixed total reserve-capacity budget, identical per-episode compute and time limits, identical initial state, and the same replayed disruption draws. The nonadaptive condition must be permitted to spend reserve capacity on the same schedule or at the same total amount as the adaptive condition; unused reserve capacity is recorded rather than silently reallocated.",
  "controls": [
    "Use identical initial states and paired, replayed disruption traces across conditions.",
    "Randomize condition order across episodes while preserving trace pairing.",
    "Include a no-shift control in which the bottleneck remains stable, to test whether any advantage is specific to shifting bottlenecks.",
    "Include instrumentation checks for reserve-budget accounting, bottleneck measurement, activation timing, switching events, and disruption-trace identity.",
    "Predefine the allocation schedule, performance metric, latency metric, switching-cost metric, and analysis rule before running the fixture."
  ],
  "observable": "Primary observable: paired difference in task performance or recovery time on shifting-bottleneck episodes. Secondary observables: performance on stable-bottleneck episodes, total reserve capacity consumed, activation latency after a bottleneck shift, number and cost of allocation switches, and disruption-related performance loss.",
  "falsifier": "The focal mechanism is falsified for this fixture if, with valid manipulation and measurement controls, the adaptive policy shows no improvement over the capacity-matched nonadaptive policy on the prespecified primary observable across shifting-bottleneck episodes, or if any apparent improvement disappears after matching and accounting for reserve consumption, activation latency, and switching cost.",
  "inconclusive_condition": "The result is inconclusive if reserve budgets or disruption draws are not matched, if bottleneck measurement or manipulation fails, if activation latency or switching cost cannot be recorded reliably, if paired traces differ, or if the prespecified primary observable cannot be computed for the required episodes.",
  "stopping_rule": "Stop after the prespecified fixed set of paired software-fixture episodes has been completed, or stop earlier if any manipulation, resource-accounting, disruption-replay, or measurement-control failure is detected. Do not stop early because one condition appears favorable.",

entries.text: The package provides multiple pairwise comparison tests for use after an omnibus analysis. It includes both parametric and nonparametric procedures applicable to factorial and block designs, allowing pairwise comparisons to be conducted in these analytical settings. The package also integrates with common scientific Python tools and provides heatmaps of pairwise test results [D1]. These heatmaps present the results of the pairwise tests; they do not establish that all hypotheses are supported. The available description identifies the package’s analytical and visualization capabilities but does not report a runtime benchmark or a numerical speedup. It likewise provides no basis for claiming that the package is universally applicable, guarantees statistically significant findings, or was the first solution of its kind. The description is a statement of software capabilities, not a report of a performed experiment.
